qualifying_updates.title: Copilot code review adds branch-tested instructions, custom setup, firewall, and separate runners
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub says Copilot code review now reads review instructions from the pull request head branch, supports additional instruction files, can use a dedicated copilot-code-review.yml setup file, runs behind a default firewall, and has runner settings split from Copilot cloud agent.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI-assisted code review practice can now validate instruction changes before merge, isolate review-agent runtime setup from coding-agent setup, and treat network access as a review-specific governance control.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Maintain review-agent instruction files as branch-testable artifacts and document review runtime/firewall configuration separately from background coding-agent setup.

qualifying_updates.title: Repository-level Copilot metrics expose coding-agent and review PR activity
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub added enterprise and organization REST endpoints that return daily per-repository pull request counts for Copilot coding agent and Copilot code review, including review suggestion counts by comment type.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Team adoption dashboards can move from user-level activity to repository-level AI-readiness, making it possible to compare where agents create, review, and merge pull requests.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Track AI-assisted pull request activity at repository granularity, with separate measures for agent-authored PRs and AI review comments.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot app usage joins enterprise and organization metrics API
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub added Copilot app fields to enterprise and organization usage reports, including distinct active app users, session counts, request counts, prompt counts, and token usage.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Operating-model reporting can distinguish IDE, app, chat, code review, and coding-agent usage instead of treating all assistant activity as one undifferentiated channel.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Separate desktop/app-agent adoption and token consumption from code-review, IDE, and coding-agent activity when measuring rollout health.

qualifying_updates.title: GitHub Mobile adds one-tap Copilot fixes from PR review comments
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub Mobile can now start Copilot cloud agent directly from Copilot code review pull request comments, either from the PR main view or from individual review comments.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Source workflows are moving toward review-comment-to-agent repair loops that start outside the desktop IDE, raising supervision, context-carrying, and final-verification requirements.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Document mobile-initiated agent repair as a handoff that still needs clear PR context, review-comment traceability, and post-agent validation before merge.

qualifying_updates.title: Cursor in Slack adds planning, progress, multi-repo environments, and cross-channel context
qualifying_updates.summary: Cursor says its Slack integration now shares a plan before starting, posts progress status, can run in named multi-repo environments, prompts when a repository switch is needed, and can read or post across channels and threads.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Chat-native agent work needs explicit planning checkpoints, multi-repository environment selection, and governance around cross-channel context access.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Treat chat-triggered coding-agent tasks as governed cross-context workflows, with early plan review and explicit repository or channel boundary changes.

qualifying_updates.title: Google Cloud publishes token-efficient software engineering principles for coding assistants
qualifying_updates.summary: Google Cloud frames token consumption as a software engineering concern for AI coding assistants, warning that context bloat increases latency, cost, forgotten instructions, and hallucination risk. It recommends reusable skills, scripts, CLI tools, read-only codebase research before edits, and task-appropriate model selection.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Context architecture and coding-agent prompts should optimize for durable reusable instructions, local tooling, and bounded context rather than repeatedly restating workflow rules in every prompt.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Add token budget and context-bloat controls to agent prompt practice, especially skill packaging, read-only discovery, and CLI-based verification loops.

qualifying_updates.title: Google Cloud demos package agent scaffolding, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, approvals, and MCP tools
qualifying_updates.summary: Google Cloud published 13 demos for Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and says installing Agents CLI into coding agents gives them skills for ADK and Agent Platform. The examples include an approval agent with PII redaction, prompt-injection defense, compliance analysis, human review, Pub/Sub events, and LLM-as-judge evaluation, plus MCP tool codelabs.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Application-pattern guidance can treat agent scaffolding, pre-LLM security screens, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and evals as one connected delivery pattern rather than separate afterthoughts.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture approval-agent architecture as a practice pattern: pre-LLM screening, explicit human review, event triggers, MCP tools, deployment, monitoring, and eval hooks.

qualifying_updates.title: Microsoft shows API-safe evaluation for agent skills
qualifying_updates.summary: Microsoft argues that agent skills calling APIs need scenario-based evaluation that avoids live costs, mutations, and nondeterministic state. It describes proxy-based API emulation that keeps production URLs in the skill while intercepting requests and resetting data for each run.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development evals should not mutate production APIs or rewrite skill URLs just to test; stable emulation can preserve shipped prompt/context shape while making tests repeatable.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Document proxy-backed skill eval harnesses as a way to preserve production-like tool context without incurring costs or changing live state.

qualifying_updates.title: TrueFoundry frames model deprecation as gateway and configuration-inventory practice
qualifying_updates.summary: TrueFoundry uses active provider deprecations to argue for model indirection, observational inventories, and staged cutovers. It notes that model IDs can hide in service configs, notebooks, CI, framework defaults, coding-agent configuration files, and third-party tools.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Coding-agent governance should inventory model identifiers outside application source code and route agent configurations through stable aliases with traffic, cost, owner, and fallback visibility.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Treat coding-agent model configuration as managed infrastructure with owner-aware inventory, deprecation drills, central aliases, and eval-gated rollback paths.

qualifying_updates.title: Security Boulevard syndicates MCP security roadmap emphasizing schema manipulation and connection inventory
qualifying_updates.summary: A syndicated Gopher Security post argues that MCP's dynamic schema discovery creates interception and schema-manipulation risks. It recommends mapping MCP connections, categorizing sensitivity, and transitioning sensitive endpoints with hybrid post-quantum controls.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: MCP governance should include connection inventory, sensitivity classification, schema-trust review, and cryptographic roadmap planning for long-lived sensitive agent traffic.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Add MCP connection inventory and schema-manipulation risk checks to tool-governance guidance, while routing broad MCP ecosystem background upstream.
